  year_added x status, and last_online availability:

  last_online overall span: 2026-06-25 16:46:29 .. 2026-09-23 15:44:51
  date_added  overall span: 2018-06-05 00:00:00 .. 2026-09-23 00:00:00

  KEY TEST: if last_online were a true event time, offline URLs added long
  ago would carry last_online values from long ago. They do not -- every
  populated last_online falls inside [2026-06-25, 2026-09-23]. So last_online is only
  recorded for activity inside a retention window, and the older rows are
  not a random sample of history: they are whatever the feed still holds.

  among OFFLINE rows, share with an observable last_online, by cohort:
      n_offline  n_with_lo  pct_with_lo
yr                                     
2026      42272      33881         80.1

==============================================================================
2. URLhaus -- the cohort with complete follow-up
==============================================================================
  retention window opens 2026-06-25; feed ends 2026-09-23 (89 days)

  Design: a URL is analysable only if a takedown occurring after it was
  added would have been RECORDED. That requires date_added >= the window
  start. URLs added before it can be taken down before it, and their
  event time is then missing -- which is exactly what the table above
  shows: 8391 of 42272 offline rows have no last_online.

  cohort (date_added >= 2026-06-25): n=44630 of 58310 = 76.5% of the feed

==============================================================================
5. VERDICT -- what E0 may claim
==============================================================================
  URLhaus:
    * last_online is NOT a historical event time; it is confined to a
      89-day retention window, so `last_online - date_added` across the
      full feed is a retention artefact, not a takedown latency.
    * It IS identifiable for the cohort added inside that window
      (n=44630, events=42154), with right-censoring at the feed end.
    * The feed's older rows are NOT a random sample of history -- they are
      whatever survived in the feed -- so they must not be used to
      reconstruct long-run survival.
  ThreatFox:
    * last_seen is populated for only 44533 of 105999 IOCs and confined to a
      recent window; the same restriction applies.
  Consequence: E0 is a SHORT-HORIZON takedown-latency study with explicit
  censoring, not a multi-year persistence study. Stated in the paper.
